evidence.excerpt: Hospital discharge summaries are frequently used as the primary written handover document between specialists and primary care, yet their accessibility for patients is rarely assessed. This randomised experiment compared recall and comprehension of standard discharge summaries against plain-language rewritten versions in a sample of 120 patients recently discharged from the internal medicine ward of a regional hospital in Vojvodina. Participants were randomised to receive either the standard institutional text or a version rewritten according to Serbian Ministry of Health plain-language guidelines (average SRI score 58 vs. 34). Immediate free recall (number of correctly recalled propositions) was significantly higher for the plain-language condition (M = 7.4 vs. 4.1, Cohen's d = 0.89). A two-week follow-up telephone interview showed that medication adherence intent did not differ significantly between groups. The study concludes that readability improvements substantially help patients understand their immediate care instructions but that additional behavioural supports are needed to sustain adherence intentions over time.
